reasoning: Recent coverage focuses on New Hampshire’s open 2026 Senate race rather than a 2026 presidential general-election margin in the state, and the only concrete general-election numbers are Senate matchup polls cited within forecasting/odds articles. Those sources consistently show Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas narrowly ahead of likely GOP nominee John E. Sununu by mid‑single digits, with election forecasters and prediction markets characterizing the race as "Lean D" but still competitive. No credible, state-specific 2026 presidential general-election polling in New Hampshire appeared in the last 45 days; available presidential polling is about the 2028 primary and is therefore outside the scope of the requested general-election margin. The statewide Cook PVI for New Hampshire is D+1, reflecting a slight underlying Democratic tilt structurally.

sources.name: Octagon (citing University of New Hampshire poll)
sources.details: Octagon’s New Hampshire Senate model cites a University of New Hampshire poll showing Democrat Chris Pappas leading former Republican Sen. John Sununu 49% to 42% in a 2026 general-election matchup, and notes that both its model and the prediction market overwhelmingly favor a Democratic hold in the seat.

sources.name: OddsShopper (summarizing UNH and Saint Anselm polls plus Kalshi market)
sources.details: An OddsShopper analysis of the 2026 New Hampshire Senate prediction market reports Kalshi pricing Democrats at 88¢ versus Republicans at 12¢ and describes public polling with Pappas leading Sununu by 3–6 points in recent UNH and Saint Anselm surveys, characterizing the race as closer to "Lean D" than a near lock.
sources.date_range: June 2026 (polls referenced; prices as of August 7, 2026)

sources.name: PredictionMarketsPicks (prediction market + forecaster synthesis)
sources.details: PredictionMarketsPicks reports that as of August 15, 2026 Democrats trade at 87¢ in New Hampshire’s 2026 Senate market, notes that forecasters rate the seat "Lean D," and frames the contest as a Democratic-leaning but still competitive open-seat race.

sources.name: CNN "The 9 Senate seats most likely to flip in 2026"
sources.details: CNN’s monthly Senate-race rankings list New Hampshire among the nine Senate seats most likely to flip in 2026, describing the open race to replace Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen as competitive but highlighting it—after Michigan—as one of the GOP’s better flip opportunities, implying a close contest in a Democratic-held seat rather than a clearly GOP-favored race.

sources.name: WBUR coverage of New Hampshire’s 2026 U.S. Senate race
sources.details: WBUR’s overview of the 2026 New Hampshire Senate contest describes Chris Pappas as the leading Democratic candidate and John Sununu as the leading Republican, notes that polls show both heavily favored in their September 8 primaries, and frames the general-election as a pivotal but not extreme race, without citing a specific numeric margin.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire Survey Center – 2028 presidential primary polling in New Hampshire
sources.details: A University of New Hampshire Survey Center release and related news coverage report polling of prospective candidates for the 2028 New Hampshire presidential primary (e.g., Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Pete Buttigieg) among Democratic voters, which is about a future-cycle primary rather than a 2026 general-election presidential contest in the state.
